record.paper_title: Channel Training & Estimation for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces: Exposition of Principles, Approaches, and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can hardware structures that provide near-independent control of reflection amplitude and phase be shown to work effectively for RIS-aided communication systems, rather than only in related reflectarray or metasurface settings?

evidence.quote: A few studies in reflectarrays and meta surfaces [99], [102]–[104] aim at designing structures that allow near-independent control of reflection amplitude and phase, however, their applicability to RIS-aided communication has not been established.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a wireless communication system aided by a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS): a planar array of $N$ passive (or nearly passive) reflecting elements placed between a transmitter and a receiver, where the $n$-th element imposes a complex reflection coefficient $r_n = a_n e^{j\phi_n}$, with amplitude $a_n \in [0,1]$ and phase $\phi_n \in [0,2\pi)$, on the impinging electromagnetic wave. In most current designs the achievable pair $(a_n,\phi_n)$ is coupled: the amplitude is a (typically non-monotonic) function of the phase due to the physics of the underlying tunable element (e.g., varactor or PIN-diode loaded unit cell), which limits the achievable beamforming and channel-shaping performance.

Design and analyze a unit-cell hardware structure for an RIS such that:
1. Each element $n$ can be independently tuned to any pair $(a_n,\phi_n)$ in a prescribed two-dimensional region $\mathcal{R} \subseteq [0,1]\times[0,2\pi)$, with amplitude and phase essentially decoupled across $\mathcal{R}$.
2. The design operates over a bandwidth and at carrier frequencies relevant to wireless communication (e.g., sub-6 GHz or mm-wave bands), with insertion loss, response time, and power consumption compatible with real-time RIS-aided communication.
3. Using such elements in an $N$-element RIS, one can demonstrate—analytically and experimentally—measurable gains in channel estimation accuracy, achievable rate, or beamforming flexibility for an RIS-aided communication link, compared to phase-only or coupled amplitude-phase RIS designs.

Prove (or experimentally establish) that the resulting near-independent amplitude-phase control unit cells, which to date have been demonstrated mainly in reflectarray and metasurface contexts, can be effectively integrated into and benefit RIS-aided wireless communication systems.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (2022–2025) demonstrate RIS unit cells with near-independent amplitude and phase control, including a mm-wave (28 GHz) cell with 0–0.5 amplitude tuning and full 360° phase range using combined PIN-diode and varactor structures, and sub-6 GHz prototypes showing independent amplitude/phase coding for beam manipulation. These results indicate the question is partially solved at the unit-cell and prototype level, though comprehensive integration and end-to-end communication-system gains remain an active research area.

status_evidence.title: Millimeter-Wave Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface With Independent and Continuous Amplitude-Phase Control
status_evidence.snippet: A unit cell achieves a 0–0.5 amplitude tuning range and a −180°–+180° phase tuning range at 28 GHz using a forward-biased PIN diode and reverse-biased varactor.
status_evidence.claim: Demonstrates an RIS unit cell with independent and continuous amplitude-phase control at mm-wave.

status_evidence.title: Flexible Beam Manipulations by Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface With Independent Control of Amplitude and Phase
status_evidence.snippet: Amplitude- and phase-coding patterns on the RIS array are well designed so that the deflection angles and power intensities of the scattered beams can be manipulated independently.
status_evidence.claim: Independent amplitude and phase coding has been realized on an RIS prototype enabling flexible beam manipulation.

status_evidence.title: A filtering reconfigurable intelligent surface for interference-free wireless communications
status_evidence.snippet: RIS programmable elements have reflection phase and amplitude that can be jointly controlled by adjusting the states of the varactor and PIN-diode.
status_evidence.claim: Joint amplitude-phase controllable RIS elements have been deployed for wireless communication applications.
